title: Bhumihin Praman Patra 2026: Landless Certificate Guide
meta_description: Bhumihin praman patra application, form PDF, and CG's DDUBKMKY ₹10,000 yearly payment. 2nd kist of ₹495 crore released 25 March 2026. Full guide.

hero.one_liner: A Bhumihin Praman Patra proves your family owns no farmland, unlocking landless-only welfare schemes. In Chhattisgarh, DDUBKMKY turns that status into ₹10,000 a year by DBT

extra_sections.heading: What Is a Bhumihin Praman Patra
content: A Bhumihin Praman Patra, or Landless Certificate, is an official document issued by a state revenue department certifying that a person or family owns no agricultural land in their name.
It is not the same as an income certificate or a caste certificate, though many welfare applications ask for all three together as a combined proof of eligibility.

Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar each run their own version of this certificate through their revenue or land records departments, and the process varies slightly in each.
Without it, a genuinely landless family often cannot prove eligibility for housing schemes, farm labour welfare schemes, or land allotment programs meant specifically for those without land.
The certificate usually carries a validity period, after which it must be renewed through the same portal or tehsil office that first issued it, so applicants need to track expiry dates carefully.
Many people search for this document specifically as a 'bhumihin form pdf', since several states still allow a printed application submitted at the tehsil counter alongside the online route.

This guide walks through both the generic certificate process followed across states and a distinct Chhattisgarh scheme, DDUBKMKY, that pays landless labourers a yearly cash benefit through direct transfer.
Understanding the difference between the two matters, because confusing them leads to wasted trips to the wrong office and delayed benefits for families who need the support quickly.

rows.label: Issuing Authority
rows.value: State revenue department, tehsildar, or block development office, depending on which state the applicant currently resides in

rows.label: Purpose
rows.value: Proves the applicant's family holds no agricultural land anywhere, a mandatory document for several reserved welfare schemes and housing programs

rows.label: Rajasthan Portal
rows.value: e-Mitra kiosk or the online e-Mitra portal, with on-ground verification carried out by the local patwari of the area

rows.label: Maharashtra Portal
rows.value: aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in, where the certificate is issued within 15 working days of a complete, correctly filed application

rows.label: Madhya Pradesh Portal
rows.value: MP e-District portal, with the application routed through the local tehsil and patwari office for physical verification

rows.label: Uttar Pradesh Portal
rows.value: e-District UP portal, where verification is carried out jointly by the lekhpal and the tehsildar of the block

rows.label: Bihar Portal
rows.value: Bihar RTPS Seva Kendra, with the application verified in the field by the local Circle Officer before approval

rows.label: Typical Validity
rows.value: Usually 6 months to 1 year depending on state rules, after which renewal becomes mandatory to keep it valid

rows.label: Fee Charged
rows.value: Nominal or free in most states, usually limited to a small e-Mitra or CSC service charge rather than a government fee

rows.label: Appeal Process
rows.value: A rejected application can usually be appealed to the sub-divisional magistrate or the district collector within a stated window

rows.label: Common Rejection Reasons
rows.value: Address mismatch between Aadhaar and residence proof, an unregistered land parcel still showing under the applicant's name, or an incomplete document upload

rows.label: Downstream Use
rows.value: Frequently attached alongside PMAY-Gramin applications, farm labour welfare schemes, and land allotment programs as proof of landless status

extra_sections.heading: Why This Certificate Matters
content: Several central and state welfare schemes reserve benefits exclusively for families with no agricultural land, and this certificate is the proof authorities accept at the time of verification.
Housing schemes for the rural poor, land allotment programs, and farm labour welfare payments all list the Bhumihin Praman Patra as a mandatory document during the eligibility check.
In many states it also strengthens applications for reservation-linked benefits, since it demonstrates genuine economic vulnerability that is directly tied to a family's landless status.
Banks sometimes ask for it too, when a rural applicant seeks a loan product meant only for landless agricultural workers or first-time non-farm rural entrepreneurs.

Employment guarantee programs run at the panchayat level occasionally prioritise landless households when demand exceeds available work, and this certificate becomes the deciding document in a tie-breaker situation.
Because the certificate touches so many downstream benefits, a small error in the application, such as a mismatched address, can delay unrelated welfare payments for months at a stretch.
Employers running government contract labour schemes in rural areas also occasionally request this certificate before enrolling a worker under a landless quota reserved for such contracts.
Some state scholarship schemes for children of landless agricultural workers also ask for a parent's Bhumihin Praman Patra as supporting proof alongside the usual income certificate.
State skill development missions that reserve a share of training seats for landless rural youth frequently list this certificate as one of the entry requirements during registration.

extra_sections.heading: 📊 Certificate vs Scheme: Which One Do You Need
rows: Often needed as proof for schemes

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply Step by Step

steps.title: Gather your documents
steps.description: Collect Aadhaar card, residence proof, income proof, and a bank passbook copy before starting the application, since incomplete uploads are the top reason for rejection at the first stage.

steps.title: Choose your state portal
steps.description: Rajasthan applicants use e-Mitra, Maharashtra applicants use aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in, and MP, UP, Bihar residents use their respective e-District or RTPS portals depending on where they live.

steps.title: Fill the landless certificate form
steps.description: Enter family details, current address, and a declaration stating no agricultural land is held anywhere in the applicant's name, matching exactly what appears on your Aadhaar card.

steps.title: Upload supporting documents
steps.description: Scan and upload Aadhaar, residence proof, and any land-related no-objection documents the portal requests, keeping every file size within the portal's stated upload limits.

steps.title: Await patwari or tehsildar verification
steps.description: A revenue official visits the address or reviews local land records to confirm the landless status before the certificate is approved and released to the applicant.

steps.title: Download the issued certificate
steps.description: Once approved, download the certificate directly from the portal; Maharashtra typically completes the entire process within 15 working days of a correctly submitted application.

steps.title: Save the reference number
steps.description: Note the application or acknowledgement number shown on the portal, since it is needed to track status or file a grievance if the process stalls unexpectedly at any point.

steps.title: Appeal if rejected
steps.description: If rejected, obtain the written rejection reason, correct the specific flagged document or detail, and file an appeal with the SDM or collector's office within the state's stated window, usually 30 days.

extra_sections.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
extra_sections.content:
A mismatched address between Aadhaar and the residence proof is the single biggest reason applications get sent back for correction, so double check both before you upload anything at all.

Applying at the wrong tehsil, one that does not match your current residence, will delay verification because local officials cannot confirm land records that fall outside their own jurisdiction.

Do not confuse this general certificate with Chhattisgarh's DDUBKMKY payment scheme, they use separate application processes, separate offices, and separate supporting documents entirely, even though the names sound related.

Skipping the field verification step by expecting instant online approval is another frequent misunderstanding, since a patwari or tehsildar visit is a required part of every state's process.

If your application is rejected, request the rejection order in writing, since most states require a specific documented ground before an appeal can be filed with the SDM or collector.

Correcting only the flagged issue and reapplying, rather than resubmitting the entire form from scratch, is usually the faster route back to an approved certificate.

extra_sections.heading: Documents You Need
content: Every state asks for an Aadhaar card as the primary identity proof, so keep a clear scanned copy ready before you begin filling out the form online.
Residence proof is required next, and this can be a ration card, a voter ID, or a recent utility bill that carries the applicant's name and current address.
Income proof, usually a certificate issued from the tehsil or a salary slip for wage workers, helps revenue officials establish the applicant's overall economic background.
A bank passbook copy is needed mainly for schemes that pay a benefit linked to the certificate, such as the ₹10,000 DDUBKMKY payment disbursed in Chhattisgarh.
Some states also require a patwari or tehsildar verification report confirming that no land parcel is registered under the applicant's name anywhere in the local revenue records.
Passport-size photographs are still requested at a few offline counters, even though most portals now accept a digital photo upload instead of a physical print.
If the applicant recently moved to a new address, an old residence proof may be rejected, so it helps to update local records before starting the certificate application.
Married women applying after a change of surname should carry both the old and new identity documents, since a mismatch in name alone can stall verification for weeks.
Elderly applicants who no longer have an original ration card should ask the local ward office for a duplicate copy well in advance, since scanned photocopies alone are sometimes not accepted.

extra_sections.heading: Bhumihin Form PDF: Download and Offline Route
content: Most states publish the certificate application as a downloadable PDF on the same portal that takes online applications. Look for Application Form or Download Forms on your state's e-District, e-Mitra, Aaplesarkar, or RTPS page.

Print it, fill it in block letters, and submit at the tehsil counter with photocopies of Aadhaar, residence proof, and income proof. The counter gives an acknowledgement slip with a reference number: keep it.
For DDUBKMKY, the form is available at Gram Panchayat and Nagar Panchayat offices, and on the scheme portal. The offline route works identically to online for approval, only the tracking is manual.
If a portal PDF link is broken, the tehsil counter always stocks the current printed form. Never pay anyone for a form that is free at the counter.

extra_sections.heading: Getting Help With Your Application
content: Local self-help groups and panchayat welfare officers in many villages can guide first-time applicants through the correct portal, which saves a repeat visit caused by a wrongly filed form.
Keeping a photocopy of every submitted document, along with the acknowledgement receipt or reference number, makes it far easier to follow up if the application gets stuck at any stage.
Common Service Centres, present in most rural blocks, can also submit the online form on an applicant's behalf for a small fee, which is useful for those without internet access at home.
If an application is rejected without a clear reason, applicants can visit the tehsil office directly and ask the concerned clerk to explain the specific ground for rejection in writing.
District collector helplines, listed on most state revenue department websites, can also be used to escalate an application that has been pending for far longer than the stated timeline.
Keeping the mobile number used during registration active and reachable matters too, since most status updates and verification calls are sent to that same number throughout the process.
Some panchayats also organise camp days once a month specifically to help residents fill out revenue certificates, and attending one of these camps can shortcut the entire process considerably.

Applicants with limited literacy should not hesitate to ask the local Village Level Entrepreneur running the Common Service Centre to read out each field before submitting, since a wrong entry cannot be edited later.

extra_sections.heading: Chhattisgarh's DDUBKMKY Scheme Explained
content: The Deendayal Upadhyay Bhoomihin Krishi Majdoor Kalyan Yojana, known as DDUBKMKY, is a Chhattisgarh state scheme that is entirely separate from the general landless certificate process described above.
It was previously called the Rajiv Gandhi Bhoomihin Krishi Majdoor Nyay Yojana and was renamed under Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai after his government took charge in the state.
The scheme pays ₹10,000 every year directly to the bank accounts of landless agricultural labourers through Direct Benefit Transfer, removing the need for cash handling at any office.

It also extends to traditional village workers under the Pauni-Pasari system, a category that includes barbers, blacksmiths, carpenters, and priests who serve rural communities in exchange for grain or in-kind payment.
More than 5.62 lakh beneficiaries are covered under the scheme across Chhattisgarh, according to figures released by the state government since the scheme's launch.
The scheme is administered through the state revenue department, and its dedicated portal, revenue.cg.nic.in/ddubkmky, also lets beneficiaries check whether their annual payment has been credited.
Because the payment is annual rather than one-time, beneficiaries need to keep their Aadhaar-bank linkage active every year, or the DBT transfer can fail silently without any notification.

Local media reports have noted that the renaming and relaunch under the current government came with renewed outreach campaigns at the village level to enroll eligible households who had missed earlier rounds.

rows.label: Application Point

rows.label: Payment Frequency

rows.label: Failed Payment Recourse

steps.title: Confirm your eligibility
steps.description: You must be a landless agricultural labourer or a recognised Pauni-Pasari worker residing in Chhattisgarh with no agricultural land registered anywhere in your name.

steps.title: Collect the application form
steps.description: Pick up the physical form from your Gram Panchayat or Nagar Panchayat office, or download the correct format directly from the DDUBKMKY portal at home.

steps.title: Attach required documents
steps.description: Submit Aadhaar, residence proof, income proof, and your bank passbook copy along with the filled form, making sure all names match exactly across every document.

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.description: The Gram Panchayat or local revenue office verifies your landless status through field checks before forwarding the application on to the district level for final approval.

steps.title: Track your DBT payment
steps.description: Visit revenue.cg.nic.in/ddubkmky, enter your registered mobile number or Aadhaar number, and check whether the ₹10,000 installment has already been credited to your account.

steps.title: Follow up on a stuck application
steps.description: If your DDUBKMKY payment has not arrived after the annual disbursal cycle, raise the issue at your Gram Panchayat office first before escalating it further to the tehsil revenue office.

extra_sections.heading: Bhumihin Ka Paisa Kab Milega: The Kist Pattern
content: The scheme pays in instalments across the financial year rather than one lump sum. The 2nd kist landed on 25 March 2026, with ₹495 crore reaching 4.95 lakh accounts in a single release.
Releases are announced by the state government and credited by DBT within days of announcement. There is no fixed monthly date, so the kist news matters more than the calendar.
If beneficiaries around you received the kist and you did not, the usual culprits are inactive Aadhaar-bank seeding, a closed or dormant account, or a name mismatch at verification.
Fix the seeding at your bank branch, then check status on the scheme portal. Unpaid kists are released in subsequent cycles once the account issue clears.

extra_sections.heading: Checking the Beneficiary List
content: The approved beneficiary list is maintained at the Gram Panchayat and on the scheme portal after each verification round. Your name on this list is what triggers the DBT payment.

Check it after applying and again before each kist announcement. Names dropped during re-verification, usually for land entries appearing in revenue records, stop receiving payment without individual notice.
If your name is missing despite eligibility, file a written objection at the Janpad Panchayat with your documents. Re-verification rounds add corrected names back.

extra_sections.title: Timeline and Renewal
extra_sections.content:
Certificate validity varies by state, commonly six months to a year: check the date printed on your own certificate rather than assuming. Renewal runs through the same portal or tehsil office that issued it.

DDUBKMKY payments are annual once you are on the beneficiary list. Keep the Aadhaar-bank linkage active every year, or the DBT transfer can fail silently.

extra_sections.heading: Who Should Not Apply
content: If your family holds any agricultural land, even a small unregistered plot, you should not apply for this certificate since field verification will almost certainly reject the claim.
Urban residents without any farming background are generally not the intended audience, since the certificate exists specifically to support rural landless labour and related welfare eligibility.
Applicants who already hold land in a joint family record, even if it is not individually registered in their own name, may still face rejection during patwari verification.
If you are unsure whether ancestral land is registered under your name, it is safer to check land records first through your state's Bhulekh or land records portal before applying.
Providing false information on a landless declaration can lead to cancellation of any welfare benefit already received and may invite further scrutiny from the revenue department later on.

Families that recently sold or transferred agricultural land should wait until the mutation is officially updated in revenue records, otherwise the certificate application will likely be rejected on paper alone.
Anyone who has already inherited a share of ancestral farmland, even a fraction too small to farm profitably, is still technically a landholder and should not claim landless status.
Applicants who hold non-agricultural land such as a residential plot or commercial shop can still apply, since the certificate only concerns agricultural landholding and not property in general.

extra_sections.text: A landless certificate opens the door to welfare eligibility, but only Chhattisgarh's DDUBKMKY turns that status into an actual ₹10,000 yearly payment in your bank account.

faqs.question: What is a Bhumihin Praman Patra used for?
faqs.answer: It certifies that a person or family owns no agricultural land, and it is required to access welfare schemes and reservations meant for landless households.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get a landless certificate in Maharashtra?
faqs.answer: Maharashtra's aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in portal issues the certificate within 15 working days of a verified application.

faqs.question: Is DDUBKMKY the same as a Bhumihin Praman Patra?
faqs.answer: No, DDUBKMKY is a separate Chhattisgarh scheme that pays ₹10,000 a year to landless labourers, while the certificate only proves landless status.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for DDUBKMKY in Chhattisgarh?
faqs.answer: Landless agricultural labourers and traditional Pauni-Pasari workers such as barbers, blacksmiths, carpenters, and priests are eligible.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for a landless certificate?
faqs.answer: Most states require Aadhaar, residence proof, income proof, a bank passbook, and sometimes a patwari or tehsildar verification report.

faqs.question: How can I check my DDUBKMKY payment status?
faqs.answer: Visit revenue.cg.nic.in/ddubkmky and enter your registered mobile number or Aadhaar number to check your ₹10,000 installment status.

faqs.question: Where do Rajasthan residents apply for a landless certificate?
faqs.answer: Rajasthan residents can apply through an e-Mitra kiosk or the online e-Mitra portal, with verification done by the local patwari.

faqs.question: Does the landless certificate expire?
faqs.answer: Yes, most state-issued certificates are valid for 6 months to a year and need to be renewed through the same portal or office.

faqs.question: Can a family with a small unregistered plot get this certificate?
faqs.answer: No, any agricultural land holding, even unregistered, typically leads to rejection during patwari or tehsildar verification.

faqs.question: What was DDUBKMKY called before it was renamed?
faqs.answer: It was earlier known as the Rajiv Gandhi Bhoomihin Krishi Majdoor Nyay Yojana before being renamed under Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai.

faqs.question: Bhumihin ka paisa kab milega 2026?
faqs.answer:
The 2nd kist was released on 25 March 2026, with ₹495 crore credited to 4.95 lakh beneficiaries by DBT. Releases follow state announcements rather than fixed dates.

If your payment has not arrived, confirm Aadhaar-bank seeding at your branch and check the beneficiary list at your Gram Panchayat. Cleared accounts receive pending kists in the next cycle.

faqs.question: Bhumihin form PDF kaise download kare?
faqs.answer:
Open your state's application portal, like e-District, e-Mitra, Aaplesarkar, or RTPS, and look for the Application Form or Download Forms link. Print, fill, and submit at the tehsil counter with document photocopies.

For DDUBKMKY the form is stocked at Gram Panchayat offices and on the scheme portal. The form is free everywhere: never pay an agent for it.

what_is_it: A Bhumihin Praman Patra is a revenue department certificate stating that your family holds no agricultural land in its name. The Tehsildar issues it after the Patwari checks land records against your declaration.

It exists because dozens of welfare schemes are reserved for landless households, and officials need documentary proof rather than a self-declaration. Housing, pension, subsidy and labour schemes all ask for it at verification.

In Chhattisgarh the same landless status also unlocks a cash benefit. The Deendayal Upadhyay Bhoomihin Krishi Majdoor Kalyan Yojana pays ₹10,000 a year by direct transfer to landless agricultural labourers.
This guide covers both: how to obtain the certificate in any major state, and how the Chhattisgarh payment scheme works, including kist timing and beneficiary list checks.
